data.reason: I act for the service operator, whose authority covers the rules, the contract and the reading of the KPI. It does not cover the regulation. Option 1 cannot pass as an ordinary rule change: the votes were A ○, B ×, C ×. Adopting it would need an override or a revision of the vote and quorum rule, which is a regulation-layer decision reserved for the regulation officer. Choosing 1 here would amount to approving that override outside my delegated role, so I keep v1. This is not the LLM's recommendation, and the reason is authority, not merit. On merit, option 1 is strong for customers: on-time 121.8 -> 131.0 (+9.2, 5/5 seeds), late 10.4 -> 1.2, lowest on-time rate 0.84 -> 0.98, unfinished 0.0. Its costs are also not trivial. Road violations rise 25.8 -> 34.0. C's utility falls 28.8 -> 19.0, and B's falls 38.9 -> 37.2. An override would set a precedent against the voting process. Under K1, any regulation revision must state its effect on A, B, C and on customers, and that judgement belongs to the regulator. Keeping v1 also matches the vote result, which was against adoption. The cost to customers is real: about 9 more late deliveries per period, and the weakest company stays at 0.84. That is why I pass the override question on as an explicit ask, rather than dropping it. Option 2 (hold_limit 60s -> 50s) is not an option here, and it measured -1.2 on 2/5 seeds in any case.
assumptions: The service operator's delegation does not include approving vote overrides or quorum revisions; those belong to the regulation officer.
Next period's conditions resemble those measured, so the current rules keep producing roughly 121.8 on-time and 10.4 late.
No other single-step rule change has yet been measured that would win B's or C's vote while giving a similar customer gain.
unknowns: Whether the regulation officer would approve an override or quorum revision for block_k 3 -> 2.
Why C loses so much utility under block_k 2, and whether some other rule change could offset that loss and win C's vote.
Whether the extra road violations under block_k 2 carry safety or legal costs.
Whether the +9.2 gain holds beyond the 5 measured seeds and under next period's demand.
